title: The Secret of Socrates
coreMove: Open a hard conversation by asking questions the other person must say yes to, and only after several yeses raise the point you actually disagree on.

exampleSpecs.domain: a county librarian persuading a skeptical board member to approve a Sunday opening pilot
exampleSpecs.audience: a public-sector worker who has to win over a fiscal hawk without antagonizing him
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether the pilot gets funded for six months or dies in committee for another year
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the librarian asks three plain questions the board member can only agree with about who uses the library before she ever mentions Sundays, and the agreement is shown landing in his posture, not narrated

exampleSpecs.domain: a veterinary technician walking a grieving farmer through whether to put down an aging border collie
exampleSpecs.audience: someone who has to deliver a hard recommendation to a person who came in already braced to refuse
exampleSpecs.stakes: the dog's last week of comfort and whether the farmer trusts this clinic again
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the tech asks the farmer to describe what a good day looks like for the dog now, and gets him saying yes to small concrete observations until the farmer reaches the conclusion himself without being told

exampleSpecs.domain: a homeowner pushing back on a contractor who wants to skip a permit on a deck rebuild
exampleSpecs.audience: a first-time renovator who is afraid of being seen as difficult
exampleSpecs.stakes: a five-figure repair bill and a possible insurance denial three years from now
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the homeowner catches himself starting with the disagreement, stops, and instead asks the contractor questions about resale and inspections that the contractor has to nod along to before the permit comes up

exampleSpecs.domain: a high school band director negotiating practice times with a parent who wants her son pulled from Saturday rehearsal
exampleSpecs.audience: a teacher who has lost this exact fight twice already this year with other parents
exampleSpecs.stakes: the section's readiness for state finals and the parent's willingness to keep the kid enrolled at all
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the first version opens with the director defending the schedule and the parent hardening, the second version opens with three questions about what the parent values about the program, and the contrast in where the conversation ends is shown without being moralized

exampleSpecs.domain: a retired bricklayer in 1953 Brooklyn convincing his grown daughter not to sign a predatory installment contract for a new washer
exampleSpecs.audience: a reader who has tried and failed to talk a relative out of a bad decision
exampleSpecs.stakes: two years of garnished pay and a fight that could keep them from speaking
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the father resists the urge to say no outright, asks her instead what she expected the monthly cost to be and what she would do if the machine broke in month thirteen, and lets her arrive at her own pause

exampleSpecs.domain: a transit planner walking a hostile neighborhood meeting through a proposed bus lane on their main street
exampleSpecs.audience: a public servant who has been booed at the last two of these
exampleSpecs.stakes: a three-million-dollar grant that expires if the lane is not approved this quarter, and her standing in a community she has to keep working with
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: after a meeting that went badly, she walks back through the transcript and identifies the exact sentence where she asked residents to disagree before she had asked them to agree on anything, and rewrites the opening as four questions she could have led with
